inlines.text: A group of 347 people was tested for flu and the results were recorded.
The flu test results are not always accurate.
A person is selected at random from the tested group. What is the probability that their test result is accurate, to the nearest per cent?

answer.worked:
Accurate results are the 72 positive results for people with flu and the 256 negative results for people without flu.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number of accurate results}&=72+256\\&=328\\P(\text{accurate result})&=\frac{328}{347}\\\text{Percentage accurate}&=\frac{328}{347}\times100\%\\&\approx95\%\end{align*}$$
To the nearest per cent, the probability is $95\%$.
